messages.author: 399809f3f88a0581
messages.subject: Standardizing GPS fix interval
parts:
I had a question about GPS fix intervals and if there is any way to standardize this in the ctmm R package or shiny app.  In my study, I have approximately 50 animals that had GPS fix intervals ranging from 15 minutes to 2 hours.  I was hoping to standardize all of these animals so that they would have a common GPS fix interval of 2 hours.  I had two questions about this that I was hoping you might be able to assist me with: (1) if I was interested in home range sizes and differences between animals, would it be vital that all animals had the same GPS fix interval (2 hours) and (2) is there a built in function that I might be able to use in order to delete all of the GPS locations that were recorded more frequently than 2 hours?  

Thanks for the assistance!

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Standardizing GPS fix interval
parts:
Hi Cindy,

One of the benefits of working in continuous time is that you don't have to discard or coarsen data.

* For variograms you want to see the dt option covered in the vignette:

https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/articles/variogram.html#irregular-sampling-schedules

* Model fitting "just works", assuming the model is appropriate over the given scales.

* For home-range estimation you want to weight the times instead of discarding them:

https://esajournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/eap.1704

https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/articles/akde.html

https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/reference/bandwidth.html

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Standardizing GPS fix interval
parts:
Hi Christie,

Yes, that is the advantage of continuous-time models. You can make biological inferences across different sampling schedules. The estimates derived from the coarser data will just have larger uncertainties.

Best,
Chris
